title: He didn’t fall overnight.
paragraphs:
He didn’t fall overnight.
He drifted—inch by inch—until God’s voice felt… distant.

Pride doesn’t shout.
It whispers, “You’re fine.”
And that’s how it blocks everything heaven wants to do in you.
Here are 6 ways pride quietly shuts the door on God’s work:

1. Pride rejects correction.
You stop listening. Even when truth is right in front of you.
The Bible says in Proverbs 12:15 — “The way of fools seems right to them, but the wise listen to advice.”
Pride says, “I already know.”

2. Pride hides sin instead of healing it.
You manage your image instead of your soul.
But Psalm 32:3 shows the cost — silence leads to spiritual decay.
What you hide, God cannot heal—until you bring it into the light.

3. Pride resists dependence on God.
You pray less. You strive more.
You start living like it all depends on you.
But John 15:5 is clear — “Apart from Me, you can do nothing.”

4. Pride steals the glory.
God moves… and you take the credit.
Slowly, your heart shifts from worship to self-promotion.
And that’s dangerous ground.

5. Pride blocks repentance.
Not because you don’t sin—
…but because you won’t admit it.
1 John 1:8 — “If we claim to be without sin, we deceive ourselves.”

6. Pride resists grace itself.
This is the deepest danger.
Because James 4:6 says it plainly:
“God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble.”
Let that sink in.
Opposes.

Not ignores.
Not delays.
Opposes.
But here’s where grace walks in—

God is not waiting to crush you.
He’s waiting for you to come low.

Because humility isn’t humiliation.
It’s the doorway to restoration.

The moment you surrender, heaven responds.
The moment you confess, grace floods in.
The moment you decrease, Christ increases.
And Jesus?

He didn’t cling to status.
He humbled Himself—even to the cross (see Philippians 2:8).
That’s your Savior.

Not proud.
Not distant.
But reaching for you—even now.

So drop the mask.
Release the control.
Come back low… and watch God move again.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
